subject: Chemistry
source: Edexcel (Pearson) GCSE (9-1) Chemistry 1CH0 specification (2016 onwards) — Y10 covered topics 1–5 (Key concepts; States of matter and mixtures; Chemical changes; Extracting metals and equilibria; Separate chemistry 1).

specPoints.specTitle: Atoms, elements and compounds; relative atomic mass; chemical symbols; word and balanced symbol equations
Atomic structure: protons, neutrons, electrons; mass number, atomic number, isotopes; Bohr model
Development of the model of the atom: Dalton, plum-pudding, Rutherford alpha-scattering, Bohr, neutron discovery
Electronic configuration in shells (e.g. 2,8,8); link to position in the periodic table
Periodic table: arrangement by atomic number; metals vs non-metals; trends in groups and periods
Group 1, Group 7 and Group 0: physical and chemical properties; trends in reactivity; displacement reactions of halogens
Ionic bonding: formation of ions; dot-and-cross diagrams; properties of ionic compounds
Covalent bonding: simple molecules and giant covalent structures; properties explained
Metallic bonding: structure of metal lattice; explanation of conductivity, malleability, melting point
States of matter: particle theory; changes of state; conservation of mass; physical vs chemical changes
Pure substances and mixtures; methods of separation: filtration, crystallisation, distillation, fractional distillation, paper chromatography
Drinking water: production from sea water and waste water; uses of distillation and filtration; testing for purity
Acids, alkalis and pH: pH scale; indicators; reactions of acids with metals, bases, carbonates; neutralisation
Salts: solubility rules; preparation of soluble and insoluble salts (HT only — quantitative methods)
Reactivity series: reactions of metals with water, oxygen, acids; displacement reactions; oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer (HT only — full half-equations)
Electrolysis: molten ionic compounds and aqueous solutions; products at electrodes; half-equations (HT only)
Extraction of metals: reduction with carbon; electrolysis for reactive metals; extraction of aluminium from bauxite
Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium; effect of changing conditions on the position of equilibrium (HT only — Le Chatelier reasoning)
Industrial production of fertilisers (Haber process for ammonia): conditions, equilibrium considerations and economic compromises
Quantitative chemistry: relative formula mass; conservation of mass; reacting masses; calculations involving moles (HT only — moles, concentrations)
Concentrations of solutions in g/dm³ and mol/dm³ (HT for mol/dm³); titration calculations (HT only)
Percentage yield and atom economy; calculations and reasoning about industrial processes
Core Practical: Investigate the change in pH on adding powdered calcium hydroxide or calcium oxide to a fixed volume of dilute hydrochloric acid
Core Practical: Investigate the preparation of pure, dry hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals starting from copper(II) oxide
Core Practical: Investigate the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution with inert and copper electrodes
Core Practical: Investigate the temperature change accompanying displacement, dissolving and neutralisation reactions
